text: Any smart contract can call any other smart contract's public functions — no approval process, no partnership, no API key. That one fact is what people mean by money legos, and it's the idea this entire course is built on top of.

Deposit ETH into a lending pool and you receive an aToken — a receipt representing your deposit plus accruing interest. Because that aToken is just an ordinary ERC-20 token, a different protocol can accept it as collateral with zero custom integration work.

A flash loan borrows a large sum with zero collateral, repaid with a fee before the transaction ends. Inside one transaction, a contract can borrow, trade across two AMMs, and repay — all atomically. If repayment fails, the entire transaction reverts as if none of it happened.

Composability also means systemic risk. If one protocol's price oracle gets manipulated, every protocol that accepted its token as collateral is exposed automatically. The 2022 Mango Markets exploit worked exactly this way.
Stackable by design, and exposed by design — that's the trade DeFi makes. Next up: reading a protocol's actual docs and contracts, so you can evaluate that exposure yourself.
